newsitem.title: UZBEKISTAN: OPIC insures U.S.-Uzbek gold venture for $200 mln.
newsitem.headline: OPIC insures U.S.-Uzbek gold venture for $200 mln.

text.p: The Overseas Private Investment Corporation (OPIC) has underwritten $200 million of political risk insurance for a prominent U.S.-Uzbek gold venture.

OPIC President Ruth Harkin, in a statement made available to journalists on Friday during a visit to the Uzbek capital Tashkent, said the coverage was for U.S.-owned Newmont Gold Company, which is producing around one tonne of gold a month at Uzbekistan's Muruntau mine.
Newmont, in a joint venture with the Uzbek government, is reprocessing low grade waste ore at the mine, located 400 km (250 miles) west of Tashkent in the Kyzlkum desert.
Harkin joined a chorus of western disapproval over foreign exchange controls in the former Soviet republic.
"American investors want to know that real steps will be taken...to achieve real conversion of hard currency," Harkin said in the statement.
